full_judgment: 20. The Singapore Admiralty Court follows and applies the English common law principles in the matter of reduction of security and also in other related matters. In The "Arktis Fighter" [2001] 2 SLR (R) 157, the plaintiffs sought security for the sums of US$ 3.8m (total replacement costs of cargo) and US$ 6.5m (liquidated damages to the plaintiff's third-party contractors). The defendant vessel was arrested. The defendant applied, inter-alia, for an order to release the vessel. No evidence or argument was placed before the Court as to the value of the arrested vessel. The Admiralty Court of Singapore referred to The Moschanthy and The Polo II and observed, "There is nothing new to add to the basic point that the issue must be determined on the question of whether the security demanded by the plaintiff is excessive. How much proof is required varies, obviously, from case to case. In certain circumstances, the Court may require sight of invoices and documents of payment; and in some cases, not.  Security should be sufficient to cover the amount of the claim plus interest and costs on the basis of the plaintiffs' best arguable case, but should not normally exceed the value of the vessel arrested. Security is given in exchange of the res and unless there are sound reasons otherwise, it should only be of equivalent value."  On the question of 'best arguable case,' it was observed, "When a court considers the question of best arguable case, it ought to take a fairly broad view of the case and not limit its inquiry to the cause of action alone, and it must also take into consideration the resulting damage as part of that  case.... but the burden of proof is on the plaintiffs  to convince the Court that the amount claimed is  reasonably likely to be incurred." The Court ordered the release of the vessel on the provision of security in the sum of US$ 3.8m plus interest over three years at 8% and costs at S$ 3,50,000.
